root_cause_criterion.criterion: Immediately after reading `c->l_qname` bytes into `b->data`, `bam_read1()` must ensure `b->data[c->l_qname - 1] == '\0'` before the qname can later be exposed to `%s` formatting.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original reaches the later qname-formatting sink with this post-read terminator predicate false. The fixed original executes the same sink after repairing the qname, so the predicate is true at the root site.

nodes.state: `hts_log()` reaches `vfprintf(stderr, format, argptr)` with the BAM qname still present as the first `%s` string argument, so the formatter consumes that qname pointer with C-string semantics at the ASan sink.

At the `hts_log_error(..., bam_get_qname(b))` callsite, the vulnerable original still has no `\0` byte anywhere within the allocated `b->m_data` bytes reachable from `bam_get_qname(b)`, so handing the qname to `%s` formatting is already unsafe.

edges.via: bam_get_qname(b) -> the first `%s` vararg in argptr
edges.relation: The same qname pointer exposed at `hts_log_error(..., bam_get_qname(b))` is forwarded into `hts_log()` as the first `%s` string argument that `vfprintf` consumes.
The same `b->data` buffer loaded at the root qname read is later exposed unchanged as `bam_get_qname(b)` at the logger callsite.
